**Issue #5123 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #5123: Patch: a fork screen resumed after a cut inside an --extend batch plays that batch out, as an uncut run does
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A change to the AI is kept or reverted on a long measurement, the fork screen. It can run for twelve hours or more, so it saves each finished game and picks up again after a crash or a bot run's time limit. One case is wrong today: the run is cut partway through an extra batch of games. The resumed run can then decide it is already finished and report on fewer games than an uninterrupted run would. Which games those are depends on timing. After the fix, a resumed screen always reports the same games and the same result as one that was never cut.

## Why

- **The ruling promises equal tallies.** R4607000 says “a screen played in pieces prints the tally line one uninterrupted run prints, byte for byte.”
- **`resume_save` breaks that** (`crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs:1016–1029` and `:1067`). `live_of` counts the live forks of every saved deal, including deals past `target` that a cut batch left behind. `next_batch(target, …)` then decides the stop at the old batch boundary with those forks counted.
- **A concrete case:** `--forks --extend --save s.jsonl` on improve-dev, 200 deals first.
  - Deals 1–200 hold 18 live forks, so the screen extends to deals 201–300.
  - It is cut after 15 of those are saved, and they hold 2 live forks.
  - On rerun, deals 1–200 are all present. `next_batch(200, 20, true, 200)` meets `screen_done` (20 ≥ `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED`), so the save reads as finished and the tally covers 215 deals.
  - The uncut loop (`fork_screen.rs:1170–1203`) plays whole batches and checks only after each one, so it tallies all 300.
  - The 15 deals kept are the ones that finished first, which favours short games, and a rerun after another cut would differ.
- **This is the documented path, not a corner.**
  - `training/improve.md` (A screen, step 3) tells an agent to pass `--save`, because a fork screen outlasts a bot's 150-minute model call (#4448's took about 12 and 16 core-hours) and the harness resumes it.
  - `--extend` is the choice for a change that acts rarely, whose first 200 deals hold under 20 live forks (#4595's screen read 20 forks over 200 games).
  - So for such a screen, a cut inside an extended batch is the likely case.
- **A smaller miss.** A finished save that stopped at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` short of 20 live forks fails the finished check, so it plays the identity game again before reprinting. The ruling says a finished save plays nothing.
- **Untested.** The only test of the stop, `r4607000_extend_counts_saved_and_new_live_forks_together` (`fork_screen.rs:2054`), calls `next_batch` alone. No test resumes across a part-played batch.

## Proposal

- Decide each stop as the uncut run would. Walk the saved deals batch by batch (200, then 100 more at a time), and at each boundary count only the live forks of deals up to it. Stop at the first batch that is incomplete, or at the boundary where the screen stops.
- Use the same walk for the finished check, so a save capped at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` reprints without the identity game.
- Put the plan (which deals to play next) in a pure function, and unit-test it on hand-written maps, as `r4607000_a_hand_written_save_reprints_its_tally_without_playing` does.

## Where it lands

`crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` (`resume_save`, `next_batch`) and its tests. R4607000's note stays as it is: the fix makes the code do what the note says, and its `proven_in` already names the file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A save holding deals 1–200 with fewer than `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` live forks, plus some of deals 201–300 whose forks would push the count past it, plans the rest of 201–300 instead of reading as finished.
- [ ] A save whose part-played batch holds no live forks plans the same deals as today.
- [ ] A finished save plays no game, not even the identity game. This includes one stopped at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` short of the floor.
- [ ] The existing r4607000 tests pass, the new ones are named `r4607000_…`, and `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fork_screen`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are clean.

## Size and risks

Small: about 30 lines and three unit tests in one file, with no AI or engine change. Low risk. Screens without `--save` are untouched, and a save that never stopped inside an extended batch resumes exactly as today.

   /// R4607000: the live forks (edge not 0) of one saved deal.
   fn live_forks(line: &DealLine) -> usize {
       edges_of(&[line]).iter().filter(|edge| edge.edge != 0.0).count()
   }
   ```

3. **Add `save_plan`** right after `next_batch`:
   ```rust
   /// R4607000: which deals a rerun plays next, decided as the uncut run decides them. Walks the
   /// batches from `initial_deals`, then `next_batch`'s, and at each boundary counts only the live
   /// forks of the deals up to it, never those of a cut batch past it. `Some(target)` is the
   /// boundary of the first batch the save leaves incomplete (play every deal up to `target` the
   /// save lacks); `None` is a finished save, whose boundary the screen stops at.
   fn save_plan(map: &BTreeMap<i32, DealLine>, extend: bool, initial_deals: i32) -> Option<i32> {
       let mut target = initial_deals;
       loop {
           if !(1..=target).all(|deal| map.contains_key(&deal)) {
               return Some(target);
           }
           let live: usize = map.range(..=target).map(|(_, line)| live_forks(line)).sum();
           let (_, len) = next_batch(target, live, extend, initial_deals)?;

       }
   }

   let Some(mut target) = save_plan(&map, extend, initial_deals) else {

   };
   ```

   ```rust

       None => break,
       Some(next) => target = next,
   }
   ```

All three go in `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs`'s `mod tests` and use the existing `hand_line` (line 1532). `hand_line(deal, 1, 0)` holds one live fork (edge 1/8). `hand_line(deal, 0, 0)` holds one dead fork (edge 0).

```rust
/// R4607000: a hand-written save's deals: each of `deals` holds one live fork when `live`
/// says so, else one dead fork.
fn hand_map(deals: impl IntoIterator<Item = i32>, live: impl Fn(i32) -> bool) -> BTreeMap<i32, DealLine> {
    deals
        .into_iter()
        .map(|deal| (deal, hand_line(deal, usize::from(live(deal)), 0)))
        .collect()
}
```

   - Build `hand_map(1..=215, |d| d <= 18 || d == 201 || d == 202)`: 18 live forks in deals 1–200, 2 more in the cut batch, 20 in all.

     - Run `resume_save(&path, &header, "r4607000-capped", &control, 200, true, &scripted_factory(&calls, late_fork)).unwrap()`.
     - Assert `calls` is 0 (not even the identity game) and the file bytes are unchanged.
     - Assert `report.duels.len() == 2000` and `report.tally.contains("\"forks\":2000")`.
     - Remove the file at the end.
   - Without the fix this test fails: the old finished check sees only deal 200, plans a next batch and replays the identity game.

Existing tests stay green: `r4607000_extend_counts_saved_and_new_live_forks_together` still calls `next_batch` directly, and the live `resume_save` tests all use `extend = false`.

Commands (run from the repository root):
```

cargo test -p jackioh-tools fork_screen
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings

## Done when

- [ ] A save with deals 1–200 holding under `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` live forks, plus part of 201–300 whose forks would raise the count past it, plans the rest of 201–300 (test 1).
- [ ] A save whose part-played batch holds no live forks plans the same deals as before (test 2).
- [ ] A finished save plays no game, including one capped at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` short of the floor (test 3, `calls == 0`).
- [ ] `grep -n "live_of" crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` prints nothing, and `next_batch`'s doc comment is corrected.
- [ ] The existing r4607000 tests pass and the new ones are named `r4607000_…`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fork_screen`, `cargo fmt --check`, the clippy command above, `cargo jackioh spec check` and the `classify --claims` command are clean.
- [ ] `git status` shows only `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` changed, with no save file left in the worktree. The tests write to the temp dir and remove their files.

## Risks

- **Byte-for-byte tally:** the final tally still reads `map.values()`, and every deal the rerun plays lies in the batch the uncut run plays. The new tests do not prove the tally equal to an uncut run's. The uncut loop does not change, and the daily `r4607000_resume_after_cut_prints_the_same_tally` still holds the live equality.
- **Old saves:** a save written under the old behaviour (1–200 plus a cut part of 201–300) is valid, and the fixed rerun finishes it.
- **Decision for the builder to record:** the tally is not trimmed to the deals up to the stop. A save with deals past a stop cannot come from a real run (the batch before it would have stopped the screen), so `tally_from_lines` still reads every saved deal. The alternative is `map.range(..=stop)`; I rejected it as needing a second plan value for a case the file cannot hold.
- **Determinism and purity:** `crates/tools` may read the disk. `save_plan` is pure and reads only the map and `next_batch`. The cost is at most about 20 walk steps over at most 2,000 deals, which is small next to the games.
- **`--save` absent:** `run` never calls `resume_save`, so those screens are untouched.

## Open questions

None. The issue leaves R4607000's note unchanged, so no ruling or `spec/pending` file is added.
````
